doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The train to California in a drawing room
summary: His stepfather, a Pullman porter, puts him in a drawing room on the City of New Orleans to Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So, and then we figured out there was a connection with him. I didn’t know what it was. It was spiritual, I felt it, and Booker and I were listening to this stuff all the time. And so when I got to USC... Here’s another thing: Because I got run out of town so early, and I didn’t get to go to Chicago or New York with my peers.
That’s where I was headed to, but my stepfather was a car salesman and a Pullman porter, and so he could get me on the train he ran to Cali.
The City Of New Orleans, they would run - that train would run out to Cali.
And so he put me in a drawing room.
You know I had a whole drawing room, they’d bring me my stuff, you know! So I was lodged, I didn’t know what that was.
You had garde - as Max Roach said, you had garde noire.

Right! [Laughs] You know, so that’s how I came to Cali. You know, I thought, “Wow, ok, I can dig this!” And that... I don’t eat that stuff anymore, but that ham and bacon on... and the eggs on the train. Man, those brothers would cook that stuff, that stuff would put a... whoo, it was so good! But anyway, so what did you just ask me?
Well we were talking about Halsey Stevens and about Bartok.
